title: Pog and Pip's Pebble Quest
markdown:
Pog the little goblin lived in a snug hollow under the roots of an old pine tree, right by the Whispering Woods, a place he knew better than his own mossy hands. He did not dream of big adventures. He loved the quiet rustle of leaves, the smell of damp earth, and his best friend, Pip.

Pip was no ordinary friend. A bat, small and soft like velvet, ears that twitched at every tiny sound. His favourite thing was napping in Pog’s pocket. Sometimes he found a particularly cozy nook in Pog’s collection of shiny pebbles. Today he needed a new napping spot, something extra-special. Pog had a plan. The most perfect, shiniest pebble in the whole wide world. That was his quest.

“Come on, Pip,” Pog whispered, voice as soft as a sigh of wind. Pip stirred and gave a sleepy chirp. Pog held out his hand. Pip fluttered and landed on his wrist.

They walked a familiar rocky path. Pine needles tickled Pog’s nose. The sun peeked through the branches of Owlglass Mountain and made dappled patterns on the forest floor. A perfect day for finding pebbles. Suddenly a loud odd sound floated towards them. Not happy bird-chirp. Not grumpy owl-hoot. Arguing. Very loud. Very muddled.

Pog’s ears flattened. A tremor rippled through his mossy skin. A shiver, not of cold but of worry. Loud noises always made him feel wobbly. Paws clammy against his wrist. His deepest unease was loud unpredictable noise, and this sounded like a whole lot of both. He almost turned back. Heart thumped like a trapped moth. Pip nudged his ear with a tiny nose. Don’t worry. I’m here.

The arguing grew louder from a small clearing just ahead, a place Pog had never explored. He took a deep breath. Damp earth suddenly was not so comforting. He really wanted Pip’s perfect pebble, but a feeling tugged him forward. Just a little peek, Pip, he murmured. He crept to the edge of the trees. Green toes sank softly into moss.

Two figures were talking very loudly. Elara, a witch with a pointy hat that seemed to have a mind of its own, tipping sideways as if about to fall. Cinnamon and elderflower, usually pleasant, a bit sharp today. The other was Taliesin, a wizard whose glasses kept sliding down his nose. He pushed them back with an impatient flick. Old parchment and a hint of dried lavender.

“It’s my Moonpetal Dust,” Elara declared, voice high and clear, sapphire nail pointing at a patch of disturbed earth. “I left it by the bubbling cauldron, right next to the toadstools.”

“Nonsense, Elara,” Taliesin huffed, glasses up again. “That was my shimmer-root. I need it for my invisibility potion. You’ve misplaced it again, just like the griffin feather last Tuesday.”

Pog watched, eyes wide. He had never seen a witch and a wizard argue. They were not truly frightening. Just very loud. They stomped. Pebbles skittered. Hands waved like windmills. Voices boomed, echoing off the trees. Pog’s ears ached. He wanted to hide, to burrow until the noise stopped. He squeezed his eyes shut. The bright daylight felt too much. Pip gave a soft encouraging chirp from his shoulder. A small sound in the din.

Then Pog noticed something. Pip, usually so calm, was flapping. Velvet head tilted. Large ears swiveled. He was looking not at the bickering pair but at a low branch. A small pale flower dangled there, petals shimmering faintly in a sunbeam. Elara and Taliesin were so busy looking at each other, and at the ground, they had not seen it.

“Um,” Pog began. A tiny squeak, barely heard above the shouting. He pointed a wobbly finger. Hand trembled. “Is… is that it?”

They stopped. They turned. Eyes wide with annoyance followed his finger. Elara gasped. Her pointy hat wobbled. “My Moonpetal Dust.” Taliesin blinked. “Well, I’ll be. It does look remarkably like my shimmer-root ingredient, doesn’t it?”

Silence fell, heavier than any argument. They looked at the flower, then at each other. Sheepish looks, like children caught with jam on their noses. Relief washed Pog until his knees felt weak. The loud noises had stopped.

“Oh, dear,” Elara said. Her hat wobbled as she chuckled, tinkling bells. “We were quite worked up, weren’t we? Making a dreadful fuss.”

“Indeed,” Taliesin admitted. He sighed, and all his pomposity seemed to float away. “My apologies, Elara. And yours, young… uh… goblin.”

Pog shuffled. Soft moss cushioned his steps. Now they were looking at him. A blush crept up his green cheeks. He wished he had a nice shiny pebble to offer, something smooth and reassuring to make things less awkward.

“It’s Pog,” he managed, still quiet. “And this is Pip.”

Elara smiled, warm and crinkly, reaching her eyes. The hat settled a little. “Well, Pog and Pip, you’ve saved the day. We couldn’t find it anywhere. The invisibility potion would have been quite ruined without it.”

Taliesin nodded. Respect in his voice. “A very clever find. Though I suppose we owe you something for intervening in our little disagreement. You were quite brave to speak up.” His gaze was steady.

Pog’s mind raced. What could he give? No shiny pebbles in his pockets. He did have a small pouch of his special dandelion sweets, his absolute favourite, made with sunshine-sweet honey and the finest dandelion fluff. He clutched the pouch. Its roughness felt familiar and comforting. Sharing meant fewer for quiet afternoons with Pip. He pictured the chewy goodness melting, honey, the delicate puff dissolving, a moment of pure quiet joy saved for just them. A small pouch. For Pog it felt like a large offering. He pictured Pip’s happy chirps when they shared a sweet, the tiny flutter as Pip nibbled. That made it harder. Another deep breath. Pine needles suddenly very reassuring.

He pictured Elara and Taliesin no longer arguing, perhaps sharing a chuckle over a simple offering. That made up his mind. “Here,” he said, holding out the pouch, leather soft and yielding. “These are dandelion sweets. They’re very good. My Mum makes them.”

They looked at the pouch, then at each other, then at Pog. Elara’s smile grew warmer. “That’s very kind, Pog. Thank you. What a thoughtful gesture.” Taliesin nodded, a twinkle in his eye that had not been there before. “Indeed. A true act of generosity. Your Mum must be very proud.”

They each took a sweet. Fingers brushed gently against Pog’s. To his surprise they did not eat them at once. They put them carefully in their own pouches and patted them secure. “We shall savor these,” Taliesin said, the earlier huffiness gone.

“Thank you, Pog,” Elara added, softer now, a gentle breeze. “You showed us a better way. Sometimes you just need a little kindness to stop the bickering.”

Warmth spread through him, much nicer than the wobbly fear. He and Pip, with a friendly nod to the now much calmer witch and wizard, turned back along the rocky path. The arguing had stopped completely. A quiet companionable murmur had taken its place, two old friends reminiscing.

Back in his cozy hollow, Pog found the most perfect smooth grey pebble he had ever seen. It gleamed under the pine needles, cool and solid. He placed it carefully in Pip’s newly prepared napping hollow. Pip nudged it with his nose, chirped with delight, and curled up, a small velvety ball of happiness. Pog watched. A contented sigh. Pine needles sweet and familiar.

Later, as stars began to prick the twilight, he heard a distant happy hooo-hooo from an owl. A loud sound, a call across the darkening woods, and he did not flinch. Even loud noises, like the witch and wizard’s argument, could sometimes lead to something good, something kind, something that made the world a little warmer. He snuggled deeper into his hollow, Pip a warm weight on his chest, and listened to the gentle sounds of the Whispering Woods, feeling safe. A quiet curiosity had taken the old flinch’s place.
characters: Pog (the young goblin), Pip (velvet pet bat)
